---
title: "Ice sheets at the Last Glacial Maximum"
---

Maps of the Northern Hemisphere ice sheets and of Antarctica 20 000 years ago,
at the Last Glacial Maximum, in the styles of the present-day posters: the
ice-surface elevation and the bed topography, with the present-day coastline
and ice margin for comparison. The ice sheets come from the PaleoMIST 1.0
reconstruction (Gowan et al., 2021[^pm]). Its changes since then in ice, surface
and bed (including the lower sea level) are added to present-day topography
(ETOPO 2022 and BedMachine Antarctica v4), see [Data & methods](about.qmd#paleo-maps).

{{< include _gallery_paleo.md >}}

## Key numbers compared with published estimates

Ice volume and sea-level equivalent more than today, per ice sheet, computed on
the map grids, compared with the values of PaleoMIST at 20 000 years ago
(`volume_sorted.txt` of the data set).

| | Map: volume (10⁶ km³) | Map: sea-level equiv. (m) | PaleoMIST: volume (10⁶ km³) | PaleoMIST: sea-level equiv. (m) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| North America, Greenland, Iceland | 31.5 | 75.0 | 30.7 | 77.3 |
| Eurasia | 7.9 | 17.8 | 7.3 | 18.5 |
| Antarctica | 5.9 | 11.8 | 3.9 | 9.7 |
| Patagonia | — | — | 0.3 | 0.7 |
| Total | 45.4 | 104.7 | 42.2 | 106.3 |

- The sea-level equivalents of the maps count the ice above flotation, as on
  the present-day posters; those of PaleoMIST are its ice volume over an ocean
  of 3.61 × 10⁸ km² (ice density 910 kg m⁻³).
- The Northern Hemisphere numbers agree with PaleoMIST within a few percent.
  For Antarctica, the PaleoMIST thickness grids themselves give 6.4 × 10⁶ km³
  more ice than today on the map grid, close to the map; the smaller volume in
  `volume_sorted.txt` is not explained by the method of the maps.
- PaleoMIST has less ice than earlier reconstructions: 42.2 × 10⁶ km³ and a
  maximum sea-level fall of 116 m (Gowan et al., 2021), against
  53 × 10⁶ km³ and 130–135 m from far-field sea-level data (Lambeck et al.,
  2014[^lam]).

[^pm]: Gowan et al. (2021), A new global ice sheet reconstruction for the past 80 000 years, *Nature Communications* 12, 1199, doi:[10.1038/s41467-021-21469-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-21469-w); data: doi:[10.1594/PANGAEA.905800](https://doi.org/10.1594/PANGAEA.905800).
[^lam]: Lambeck et al. (2014), Sea level and global ice volumes from the Last Glacial Maximum to the Holocene, *PNAS* 111, 15296–15303, doi:[10.1073/pnas.1411762111](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1411762111).
